author: Ismael Valenzuela
text: Everyone's excited about agentic AI systems like #OpenClaw. There's huge opportunity there, no question about it, but also huge risk. The problem is that most orgs are still trying to govern these agents like a chatbot. Of course that only works until the AI stops answering questions and starts doing things like calling APIs, changing configs, browsing admin panels, and making decisions. At that point, the risk isn't what the model says — it's what the agent is allowed to do. Treat AI systems as enterprise actors with bounded authority, not IT tools.
suggestedEngagement: Add specifics on what 'bounded authority' looks like in practice — just-in-time credentials, task-scoped permissions, and a kill switch as the minimum bar
Ask what governance frameworks he's seen actually work at scale — NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative is putting out guidance but enterprise adoption lags significantly
Share the angle that the real gap is observability: most teams can't even enumerate which agents are running, let alone what permissions they hold — governance without visibility is theatre

author: Dan McAteer
text: Harness engineering is as important as model capability scaling. AI Agents are 50% a harness story. 'Natural-Language Agent Harnesses' proposes moving harness logic out of code and into the native language of LLMs: Natural Language. Turns the agent harness into a portable, inspectable artifact.
suggestedEngagement: Engage on the portability claim — natural-language harnesses are easier to audit but harder to version-control and diff; ask how he thinks teams will manage harness drift at scale

Share experience building production agent harnesses where the bottleneck wasn't model capability but context architecture — ask if he sees natural-language harnesses solving the context window constraint too
Challenge gently: moving harness logic into natural language shifts correctness guarantees from the type system to the model — does he trust that tradeoff in high-stakes enterprise deployments?
